entries.subject: VLTI/PIONIER April-May 2014 H-band visibilities, JMMC OiDB (Montargès et al. 2017)
entries.finding: The OiDB holds 23 calibration-level-2 files from the nights of 23 and 29 April and 4 and 7 May 2014 on three configurations (longest projected baseline 139 m): 1470 squared-visibility and 763 closure-phase channel rows, the JMMC pipeline's automated product. The paper never imaged them; its best models reach reduced chi-squared 25 to 44 and it reports that the star differs between the three spectral channels. SQUEEZE at the pinned commit on the merged set, started from a 37.38 mas disc, stalls at reduced chi-squared 30 with the Betelgeuse recipe and 15.5 with 10,000 elements over 8,000 iterations, never reaching burn-in; the compact-array night alone (1080 rows, five hours, one configuration) stays at 18.7; only the 7 May night (318 rows) converges, at 2.2, to a disc without resolved features. A uniform disc fits the merged set at reduced chi-squared 50,000. No image from these files is cast.
entries.revisitWhen: A reconstruction from these or later interferometric data that converges near reduced chi-squared 1 and resolves more than a uniform disc.

entries.subject: VLTI/AMBER aperture-synthesis images in the CO lines and the K-band continuum (Ohnaka et al. 2013, 2017)
entries.finding: The CDS deposit for Ohnaka et al. (2013), J/A+A/555/A24, holds two animated GIF movies, not image data; the 2017 Nature paper has no deposit found at the CDS. The AMBER observations in the OiDB are calibration level 0 (raw). Without a published image file or calibrated visibilities, nothing is cast.
entries.revisitWhen: The authors deposit the continuum image as FITS, or calibrated AMBER OIFITS of the 2009, 2010 or 2014 runs appear in the OiDB.

entries.subject: Rotation axis, period and prime meridian
entries.finding: No publication measures the rotation axis or period of Antares; Ohnaka et al. (2017) map atmospheric velocities without one. The object uses the display-orientation record: the axis shown is celestial north in the plane of the sky and the display meridian faces the Earth at the scene epoch, both labelled as a convention.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured position angle of the rotation axis is published.

entries.subject: Distance
entries.finding: Hipparcos 5.89 +/- 1.00 mas (van Leeuwen 2007), 170 pc, is adopted; the star is too bright for Gaia. The 17 percent parallax uncertainty moves the physical radius by the same fraction and nothing else in the scene.

entries.subject: VLTI/GRAVITY K-band spectro-interferometry, June 2023 (ESO programme 111.24K0, PI Ohnaka)
entries.finding: The ESO archive serves 57 pipeline-reduced GRAVITY products at Antares, found by an ObsCore query on 2026-09-21, public since June 2024: 13 June 2023 on the compact array (to 34 m, DUAL), 18-20 June on the medium array K0-G2-D0-J3 (to 104 m, SINGLE) and 27 June on the large array (to 129 m, DUAL), high spectral resolution. Three arrays in two weeks reach about 1.8 mas against a disc of about 40 mas, some 20 resolution elements, comparable to the Betelgeuse MATISSE image. The products are uncalibrated (VISCAL UNCALIBRATED) and need the pipeline calibration step (gravity_viscal) against the archived calibrators (eps Sco on 12 June, omi Sco on 18 June); no raw reduction is needed. Whether the DUAL-mode files track on Antares itself or on Antares B is not checked, and no published GRAVITY image of Antares exists to compare against. The ESO programmes 109.22WQ.002 (one night, 2022) and 111.24LM (monthly compact-array monitoring, 2023) are thinner.
entries.revisitWhen: Calibrate the June 2023 products with gravity_viscal, pin them, and test an image reconstruction against the medium and large array coverage.
